summary:
The D.C. Council is advancing new restrictions on ballot initiatives, while statehood advocates point to recent federal interventions in the District as evidence for why local autonomy matters. A senator has pledged to prioritize D.C. statehood, and advocacy groups are marking anniversaries of federal actions—including a federal takeover and National Guard deployment—to underscore what they see as the necessity of statehood.

Without statehood, D.C. residents have no voting representation in Congress, and Congress can override any law the District passes.

articles.title: D.C. Council Moves to Put New Limits on Ballot Initiatives
VIDEO: Senator Slotkin Commits to Making DC Statehood a Top Priority
One Year Later, DC Vote Says Federal Takeover Underscores the Urgency of DC Statehood
One Year After President Trump Deployed National Guard Troops to Washington, D.C., Statehood is More Important Than Ever
